title: Gaspar Yanga
summary: Yanga is remembered as the leader of enslaved Africans who fled into the mountains near Veracruz around 1570 and built a self-governing settlement. A Spanish force sent in 1609 failed to defeat them, and an agreement in 1618 let the community govern itself on condition that it take in no more fugitives. The town, once San Lorenzo de los Negros, is now Yanga.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on recognition: 1618 (JSTOR Daily) versus recognition as a free town on 3 October 1631 (Mexico Desconocido). The 1570 escape is the date both pages give.

where.modern_name: Yanga (town), municipality of Yanga, Veracruz, Mexico (pinned to the town named for him; the maroon settlement began in the mountains near Veracruz)
where.historical_name: San Lorenzo de los Negros (later San Lorenzo de Cerralvo), the settlement now called Yanga

importance.justification: Led a maroon community that negotiated self-government in colonial Mexico; remembered as an early liberator in the Americas.
